meta.scenario: tech house loop roll on groove outro — 8-bar loop creates rhythmic tension and extends the window while T2 blends in; loop for effect not just extension
meta.source: Warehouse Project Manchester 2018 — Denis Sulta closing set
meta.t2_title: All That I Want Is You

transition_arc: T1's outro has only 8 bars of clean low-energy material (bars 72–80) before near-silence. A standard 16-bar blend cannot fit: there are only 8 bars of usable runway. The solution is a loop on T1's last 8-bar percussion phrase (bass already stripped, drums-only at bar 72), creating an additional 8 bars of stable percussion runway. The loop also creates rhythmic texture — the repeated 8-bar phrase builds a hypnotic tension that makes T2's groove arrival feel like a release. Loop fires at bar 72, adds 8 extra bars (one repeat), giving bars 72–88 as the blend window. T2 fades in during this window. After the loop, T1 resumes from bar 80 (the near-silent tail) and fades out immediately.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 0: full tech house groove, kick+chopped vocal+bass, RMS 0.62
T1 bar 64: 8 bars before T2 fade_in at bar 72. Bass still present, drums=0.55, harmonic=0.35, rms=0.42
annotated_actions.why: Bass pre-cut 8 bars before T2 enters. Fires well before the loop starts at bar 72 — the loop phrase at bar 72 should have no bass, and this eq ensures it.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 72: drums=0.45, harmonic=0.02, rms=0.22 — percussion-only phrase, bass gone, no harmonic content. This is the ideal loop point.
annotated_actions.why: Loop the last 8-bar percussion phrase. harmonic=0.02 confirms no tonal content — the loop is transparently rhythmic. loop_repeats=1 adds 8 extra bars of runway (total window 72–88 instead of 72–80). loop_mute_tail=true silences the original track under the loop window — without this, the original track content would continue playing simultaneously with the loop, causing a doubling artifact by bar 80. After the loop, track resumes from source bar 72 + 8×1 = 80.
Kill T2 bass at fade start — prevents dual basslines during blend. EQ is persistent; will be restored at bass_swap point.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 0: clean tech house intro, kick + hi-hats, no bass, drums=0.40, harmonic=0.05
annotated_actions.why: T2 fades in simultaneously with the loop start. The stable looped percussion phrase is the ideal backdrop for T2's intro — the rhythmic regularity of the loop makes T2's incoming kick feel synchronised and intentional. drums:0.8 adds T2's kick over T1's looped percussion. other:0.5 — Camelot +1 (3A→4A) is safe for pad/chord blending. from_bar=0 because T2's intro begins from its first bar. stems={drums:0.8, bass:0.0, other:0.6} — T2 enters with 80% drums, no bass (held for bass_swap), 60% atmosphere.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 at bar 80: loop midpoint — T1 bass already removed by eq at bar 64. T2 bass about to enter.
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 8 (from_bar=0, 8 bars elapsed): bass building in, harmonic rising to 0.25
annotated_actions.why: Midpoint of the 16-bar fade window (72 + 8 = 80). T1's bass has been gone since bar 64. The swap formally releases T2's bass stem. Even though T1's sub is already silent, the bass_swap action is still required — it's what enables T2's bass stem overlay to fire. Without incoming_track field, the system skips T2's bass restore entirely.
Restore T2 bass at bass_swap point — T1 bass is now HPF-cut, T2 bass can come in.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 80: loop ends here (72 + 8×1 = 80), track resumes from source bar 80 — near silence, rms < 0.05
annotated_actions.why: After loop_repeats=1, T1 resumes from source bar 80 — the near-silent tail. A short 8-bar fade_out finishes it cleanly. CRITICAL: fade_out.start_bar=80, NOT 72. The loop resume point is 72 + 8×1 = 80. Placing fade_out at bar 72 would fire during the first loop repeat, cutting the loop short and leaving T2 underblended.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 16: full tech house groove, kick+bass+chopped elements, RMS 0.60
annotated_actions.why: T2 full groove replaces the stem-layered fade_in. Loop has ended, T1 is fading out in near-silence. from_bar = fade_in.from_bar(0) + fade_in.duration_bars(16) = 16. The audience experienced: T1 groove → looped percussion tension (8 extra bars) → T2 new groove emerging. The loop created rhythmic anticipation that makes T2's full groove feel like a payoff.
